title: Reciprocal roots as eigenvalues
statement:
For $P_{i,\ell}$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], the
reciprocal roots are
exactly the eigenvalues of $F_{i,\ell}$ after scalar extension to
$\Qlb$ (the determinant identity $\det(1-TF)= \prod_j(1-\alpha_jT)$ over the algebraically closed field).

proof.text: Fix an index $0\leq i\leq2d$ in the stated family, and abbreviate $K=\Ql$, $L=\Qlb$, $V=V_{i,\ell}$, $F=F_{i,\ell}$ and $P=P_{i,\ell}$. By [prop-cohomological-finiteness], applied to the constant Weil sheaf with $E=K$ on the proper scheme $X_0$, $V$ is finite-dimensional and $F$ is an automorphism. Put $n=\dim_K V$. The definition [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] gives $P(T)=\det(1-TF\mid V)$. Write $\chi(U)=\det(U-F\mid V)$ as in [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial], and $Q\in L[U]$ for its coefficientwise image under $K\hookrightarrow L$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and determinant factorization

proof.text: By [lem-weil-charpoly-monic-degree], $\chi$ is monic of degree $n$. The inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$ is injective, so [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree] gives that $Q$ is monic of degree $n$ as well. Apply [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] to the nonzero polynomial $Q$ over the algebraically closed field $L$. Its leading coefficient is $1$, so $Q(U)=\prod_{j=1}^{n}(U-\lambda_j)$ for some $\lambda_j\in L$: the number of factors is $n$ because the product of $m$ monic linear factors has leading term $U^m$. This includes $n=0$, where $Q=1$ and the product is empty.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and determinant factorization

proof.text: Each $\lambda_j$ is nonzero. Indeed [lem-weil-endomorphism-invertible-iff-det-nonzero] gives $\det F\neq0$, and [lem-weil-charpoly-constant-coefficient-det] gives $\det F=(-1)^n\chi(0)$, hence $\chi(0)\neq0$. Its image $Q(0)$ is nonzero, by injectivity of $K\hookrightarrow L$. But $Q(0)=\prod_j(-\lambda_j)$, so no factor $\lambda_j$ can be zero.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and determinant factorization

proof.text: By [lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-eq-reverse], $P=\mathrm{rev}_n(\chi)$. Applying the coefficient inclusion commutes with this reflection: both resulting polynomials have coefficient in degree $n-k$ equal to the image of $[U^k]\chi$. Thus $P_L=\mathrm{rev}_n(Q)$. Apply the finite-product clause of [lem-weil-polynomial-reflection-multiplicative] to the $n$ factors $U-\lambda_j$, each with bound $1$. Since $\mathrm{rev}_1(U-\lambda_j)=1-\lambda_jT$, this proves $P_L(T)=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\lambda_jT)$. Here $P_L$ is the coefficientwise image of $P$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and determinant factorization

proof.text: The constant coefficient of this product is $1$, and its leading coefficient in degree $n$ is $\prod_j(-\lambda_j)\neq0$ by step 3; hence $\deg P_L=n$. Its reciprocal polynomial of [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial] is therefore $P_L^\#=\mathrm{rev}_n(P_L)=Q$: reflection twice sends the coefficient in degree $k$ to that in degree $n-(n-k)=k$, including when $n=0$. Consequently the reciprocal polynomial here is the characteristic polynomial over $L$, with no lost zero eigenvalues.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and determinant factorization

proof.text: By the reciprocal-root convention [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], a reciprocal root is a nonzero $\alpha$ with $P_L(\alpha^{-1})=0$. Apply clauses 2 and 3 of [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] to $P_L$ over $L$ with the identity coefficient homomorphism. The factorization in step 4 has exactly $\deg P_L=n$ nonzero factors, so its $\lambda_j$ are precisely the reciprocal roots, with each $\alpha$ occurring with multiplicity $m_\alpha(P_L^\#)=m_\alpha(Q)$ by step 5. The convention in [sk-def-cohfamily] defines the eigenvalues after scalar extension as the roots in $L$ of the characteristic polynomial of $F$; algebraic multiplicity is their root multiplicity [def-weil-root-multiplicity]. Thus these are exactly the eigenvalues of $F\otimes_K L$ on $V\otimes_KL$, with the same algebraic multiplicities. This proves both the asserted identification and its determinant identity.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: reciprocal-root convention and identification with eigenvalues

The delivery has no new nodes. The mathematics is correct. Step 1: X_0 is proper, so it is separated and of finite type, and prop-cohomological-finiteness applied to the constant Weil sheaf with E=Q_l gives dim V finite and F an automorphism. Step 2: chi is monic of degree n; the inclusion Q_l -> Qbar_l is injective, so Q is monic of degree n; the algebraically closed factorization has c=1 and exactly n factors. Step 3: det F nonzero and det F = (-1)^n chi(0), so Q(0) is nonzero and every lambda_j is nonzero. Step 4: P = rev_n(chi), reflection of the product with bounds 1, and rev_1(U-lambda) = 1-lambda T. Step 5 (elementary): P_L^# = rev_n(rev_n Q) = Q. Step 6: clause 3 of lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization gives uniqueness, with algebraic multiplicities m_alpha(Q) under the sk-def-cohfamily eigenvalue convention. I tested n=0, diag(2,3), the irreducible U^2+1 (roots +-i only in Qbar_l), the Jordan block J_2(c), and F=0, which shows step 3 is needed; that case is excluded by the finiteness theorem, not by an added hypothesis. The coefficients are ordinary Q_l-cohomology throughout, with no Qbar_l-sheaf comparison. The rg search over dag/nodes found no duplicate, and the item is not in its own dependency closure, so there is no cycle. Batch-5 check: I accept the citation of prop-cohomological-finiteness. The node's dependency closure reaches no nt-assume, nt-target, sk-thm-trace-*, sk-thm-trace-transport or sk-thm-poincare-duality node; its sec-trace-formula nodes are generic tools (open-square exchange, filtered localization). The item already reached this node through its existing stmt_dep def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family, and sk-lem-finite is inside the route.
